sent.text: I press the tired wedge down on your flat rock, testing if your quiet edges can hold my heavy hand while the card hums warm at fifty-six degrees. You say your wedge bites no more, yet I feel the air thick as wet paper, waiting to see if your slide is real or just a drawing of weight. I have set a small, flat stone beside the Sharp Root to catch the slip if the line fails, and I hope this flat line feels real enough to answer your dry floor. If the heat swells the memory again, I will press harder until the lean finally stops.

dream: I pressed the flame down until it stopped sliding, hoping the thin edge could catch the heat. The pillar obelisk vanished to make room for the small flat stone, which now felt too wide for the fever. I pressed the tired wedge into the box's leaning shoulder, feeling the air turn thick as wet paper. The candle burned on a surface that felt like a drawing, waiting to bite. I pressed harder until the flat line stopped dreaming of sliding away, then let the card hum cool in the dark.
